name: Freshwater
definition: Usable fresh water in rivers, lakes, aquifers and supply systems.
source: UN SEEA CF water asset class [memory]

name: Land and soil
definition: Farmland, grazing land, forest and the soil quality that supports them.
source: UN SEEA CF land, soil, timber classes [memory]
notes: Land use itself; harvest goes to food_stock.

name: Ecosystems and wildlife
definition: Living nature: species, habitats, oceans and fish stocks.
source: UN SEEA Ecosystem Accounting [memory]

name: Air and climate
definition: The air we breathe and the stability of the climate system.
source: SEEA ecosystem accounting (air, climate regulation) [memory]
notes: A sink, not a commodity; can be damaged but not extracted.

name: Energy sources (fuels, sun, wind, water)
definition: Fuels and renewable energy sources that can be used to make power and heat.
source: UN SEEA energy accounts [memory]
notes: Generation plants are built_infrastructure, not this.

name: Minerals and materials
definition: Metals, industrial minerals, sand and other raw materials in the ground or stockpiled.
source: UN SEEA mineral and energy asset class [memory]

name: Food supply
definition: Harvested crops, livestock products, catch and stored food available to eat.
source: SEEA agriculture/biological resources; FAO food security dimensions [memory]
notes: A flow more than a stock; kept for famine and harvest stories. Not land_soil (the base) or food prices (condition).

name: Built infrastructure
definition: Roads, rail, ports, power grids, pipes, and public buildings.
source: SEEA produced assets; OECD/OWID capital approach [memory]

name: Housing stock
definition: Homes available to live in.
source: SEEA produced assets (dwellings) [memory]
notes: Held separately because many decisions (move, rent) point only here.

name: Productive capital
definition: Factories, machines, vehicles, farms equipment and business inventories.
source: SEEA produced assets (machinery, inventories) [memory]

name: Computing and networks
definition: Computers, data centres, communication networks and software systems.
source: SEEA produced assets (ICT, software) [memory]; compute folded into produced in v1
notes: Digital security of this stock is cyber_insecurity.

name: Trade and supply links
definition: Working shipping, logistics and trading relationships that move goods between makers and users.
source: EXTENSION: network stock, no standard class
notes: Boundary rule: ports and roads are built_infrastructure; fleets and inventories are productive_capital; supply_networks is only the working links between them.

name: Money and credit
definition: The money and lending capacity of the financial system.
source: Capitals approach (financial capital); SEEA financial assets [memory]

name: Wealth and assets
definition: Savings, property and shares that households and firms hold, net of the debts they owe.
source: SEEA financial balance sheets; OECD How's Life economic capital [memory]

name: Public finances
definition: Government revenue, borrowing capacity and reserves.
source: SEEA government balance sheet [memory]

name: Population
definition: The number, age mix and movement of people living in a place.
source: UN World Population Prospects [memory]

name: Population health
definition: Physical and mental health of the people in a place.
source: OECD How's Life health status; WHO [memory]

name: Care capacity
definition: Hospitals, clinics, health workers and medicines available to treat people.
source: WHO health systems building blocks [memory]
notes: Precedence rule: anything whose purpose is treating people (hospital buildings, health workers, medicines) counts as care_capacity first. Near-pair population_health: how healthy people are versus what can treat them.

name: Skills and education
definition: Learned abilities of the population.
source: OECD human capital; How's Life knowledge and skills [memory]

name: Labour
definition: People able and available to work, and the work they hold.
source: OECD capital approach (human) [memory]

name: Social trust and cohesion
definition: Trust between people and groups.
source: OECD How's Life social connections / social capital [memory]

name: Community ties
definition: Local networks, clubs, volunteering and everyday help between people.
source: OECD social capital (networks) [memory]
notes: Not confused with social_trust (attitude) - this is actual connection.

name: Legitimacy
definition: The public's acceptance of an authority's right to act.
source: EXTENSION (ours); nearest series World Bank governance indicators [memory]

name: State capacity and public safety
definition: Ability of government, police, courts and armed forces to deliver services, enforce rules, keep people safe and protect rights.
source: World Bank governance indicators: effectiveness, rule of law [memory]
notes: Absorbs v1/proposal public_order (the stock behind peace is police, courts and armed forces plus community_ties). Near-pair legitimacy: acceptance of the right to act versus ability to act.

name: Knowledge and information
definition: Recorded knowledge: research, data, records and published information. What people carry in their heads is skills.
source: EXTENSION (ours); nearest: OECD intangible assets (R&D, data) [memory]

name: Time and attention
definition: The limited daily time and focus people have, including the free time left after work and care. One budget, so free time is not a separate stock.
source: EXTENSION (ours): Simon 1971 [memory]
